result.title: Kierston & KierstonBench: Simulation of Allentown, PA and Evaluation of Language Models in Crime Investigation and Surveillance Tasks
result.summary: Large language models are candidates for collecting and analyzing records in criminal investigations and mass surveillance. Their capability and accuracy in this work cannot currently be measured. Real deployments lack the ground truth needed to score a model's conclusions, and no benchmark evaluates these capabilities in a simulated environment. We present Kierston, a city-scale simulation engine, and KierstonBench, a benchmark that tests these capabilities against known simulated events. Kierston models approximately 125,000 residents of Allentown, Pennsylvania, generating their daily activities and the telecommunications, financial, administrative and license-plate records that surveillance and investigative systems collect about them. These records derive from a common behavioral timeline and are distributed across sources representing separate providers. Models investigate through a restricted records interface, linking observations across sources without access to the underlying simulation. The benchmark comprises 32 task families covering record linkage, routine reconstruction, incident investigation and assessment of deceptive accounts. In an evaluation of sixteen language models, most could not perform records investigation and submitted identifications the records did not support. A small number of frontier models solved most of the tasks and abstained when evidence was insufficient. In some cases these models still fell for common deceptions and assumptions, and none replaced an investigator.

AI.brief_summary: 提出城市尺度模拟引擎 Kierston 与配套基准 KierstonBench，基于约 12.5 万居民模拟出的电信、金融、行政与车牌等分源记录，用已知真实事件评测语言模型在多源记录关联、日常轨迹重建、事件调查与欺骗识别上的能力，发现多数模型无法完成证据支撑的推理，少数前沿模型多数可解并会在证据不足时弃答。
AI.relevance_reason: 受限证据接口、多源观测关联与「证据不足则弃答」的设计可供核查 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 决策与视觉证据筛选的评测构造，但其为纯文本、无 latent 状态与视觉输入，联系较远。
